Smoothmoves Removalist & Storage is a well-established Sydney-based removals, packing and storage company providing tailored relocation and secure storage solutions for residential and commercial clients. With experienced teams, modern equipment and customer-focused service, the company is committed to delivering efficient, reliable and stress-free moving experiences.

As a Logistics Analyst at Smoothmoves Removalist & Storage, you will be responsible for analysing transport and storage operations, improving logistics performance, optimising resource utilisation and supporting the delivery of high-quality relocation and storage services. This position requires strong analytical ability, excellent organisational skills and a continuous improvement mindset.

Responsibilities and Tasks:

•	Analyse transport, removal and storage operations to identify opportunities to improve supply chain efficiency and service delivery.
•	Monitor logistics performance, including delivery schedules, fleet utilisation and storage capacity, and prepare analytical reports for management.
•	Evaluate freight movements, transport routes and warehouse operations to optimise productivity and reduce operating costs.
•	Develop forecasting models to support resource planning, vehicle scheduling and storage capacity requirements.
•	Analyse customer demand trends and recommend improvements to logistics and inventory management processes.
•	Monitor shipment progress, delivery timeframes and transport documentation to ensure timely and accurate customer service.
•	Assist in managing logistics records, transport documentation, invoicing and shipment tracking systems.
•	Collaborate with operations, warehouse and customer service teams to improve end-to-end removal and storage processes.
•	Identify supply chain risks, investigate service bottlenecks and recommend practical solutions to improve operational performance.
•	Ensure logistics activities comply with company procedures, workplace safety requirements and relevant transport regulations.

•	Relevant qualification.
•	Minimum 1 year experience as a Logistics Analyst.
•	Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
•	Advanced Microsoft Excel and data analysis capability.
•	Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
•	Ability to interpret operational data and recommend business improvements.

The role offers a remuneration package ranging from $79,000 – $90,000 p.a. plus superannuation for a 38-hour work week.

Ltd. is a steel solutions company that strives to keep all processing in house, with a continuous improvement policy that allows us to invest in the latest technology, machinery, handling equipment and increasing our capacities to allow us to handle all types of work from small to large offering the most economical steel solutions in Melbourne to the Australian Industry.

We are seeking an experienced and qualified Quality Assurance Officer to join and bring their expertise to our dedicated professional team in Dandenong South Victoria.

The Role
As a QA Officer, you are responsible for ensuring that all products and services consistently meet established quality standards and regulatory requirements. This involves conducting audits, performing tests, and driving process improvements. You will oversee production activities, maintain and manage documentation, investigate non-conformities, and implement corrective actions to uphold compliance with industry standards

Your Duties and Responsibilities include but are not limited to:
Conduct routine audits, inspections, and compliance checks on production lines and raw materials to ensure adherence to safety and quality standards
Create quality measurements to track improvement in products
Maintain, review, and update quality documentation, including Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), batch records, and, in some cases, product specifications
Investigate product quality issues, identify root causes, and prepare reports on non-conforming materials or processes
Manage dispatch requirements and ensure products meet customer expectations and demand
Recommend and implement corrective and preventive actions to enhance product quality and operational efficiency
Work closely with the development team to improve existing products
Ensure testing equipment is properly maintained, calibrated, and used according to protocols
Conduct audits of vendors and suppliers to ensure supplied materials meet company standards
Document quality assurance activities and create audit reports

To be considered for this role, you must have the following:
Previous work experience in quality assurance or a similar field
Working knowledge of tools, methods, and concepts of quality assurance
Solid knowledge of relevant regulatory standards
Good communication skills, both verbal and written
Excellent data collection and analysis skills
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and documentation skills, with high attention to detail.

If you have the skills required for this role and you feel this is the job for you, then apply now!
Salary: Between $79,499 and $82,000 per annum + Super

Boilermaker – Full-Time

Location: Welshpool, Western Australia 6106
Employment Type: Full-Time
Salary: $80,000 – $110,000 per annum (depending on skills and experience)

MINPROVISE INTERNATIONAL PTY LTD is a leading total solutions provider delivering specialist maintenance and shutdown services, engineering, fabrication, project services, and sustaining capital works. We also provide a comprehensive range of equipment and products, supporting the mining, oil & gas, and construction industries across Australia and internationally.

We are currently seeking experienced and motivated Boilermakers to join our growing team on a full-time basis.
About the Role

As a Boilermaker, you will be responsible for fabricating, assembling, installing, maintaining, and repairing structural steel, pressure vessels, heavy equipment, and metal components used in mining, industrial, and construction projects. You will work closely with engineers, supervisors, and maintenance teams to ensure all fabrication and welding work is completed safely, efficiently, and in accordance with engineering specifications and Australian Standards.

Key Responsibilities
•	Read and interpret engineering drawings, blueprints, fabrication plans, and technical specifications.
•	Fabricate, assemble, install, and repair structural steel, heavy machinery components, tanks, chutes, hoppers, conveyors, and other metal 
structures.
•	Mark out, cut, shape, bend, and prepare metal materials using fabrication equipment.
•	Perform welding using MIG, TIG, Stick, and Flux-Cored Arc Welding (FCAW) processes as required.
•	Carry out maintenance and repairs on plant and mining equipment during shutdowns and ongoing operations.
•	Inspect fabricated and welded components to ensure compliance with quality standards and engineering specifications.
•	Safely operate welding equipment, hand tools, power tools, cranes, hoists, and workshop machinery.
•	Identify faults, perform modifications, and recommend repair solutions where required.
•	Maintain accurate records of fabrication, repairs, inspections, and completed work.
•	Work collaboratively with engineers, supervisors, and other tradespeople to complete projects on time.
•	Assist with training apprentices and junior team members where required.
•	Follow all workplace health and safety policies, procedures, and site regulations.

Skills and Experience
•	Minimum 1–2 years of full-time experience as a Boilermaker or in a similar fabrication role.
•	Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and fabrication specifications.
•	Strong welding, fabrication, and metalworking skills.
•	Experience working with structural steel, heavy equipment, and industrial or mining plant.
•	Ability to safely operate fabrication machinery, welding equipment, and workshop tools.
•	Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving abilities.
•	Excellent attention to detail and commitment to quality workmanship.
•	Ability to work independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced environment.

What We Offer
•	Full-time, permanent employment.
•	Competitive salary of $80,000 – $110,000 per annum.
•	Opportunities to work on major mining, shutdown, and industrial projects.
•	Ongoing training and career development.
•	Supportive team environment with long-term career opportunities.

For nearly 25 years, APD Global has set the benchmark in delivering advanced, comprehensive, and specialised engineering solutions.

We have around 800 employees including our alliance contracting partners, across 15 strategically located offices in Australia (Perth, Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Adelaide, Darwin), New Zealand and Malaysia. We specialise in seamless integration across the Power Systems, Telecommunications, and Renewable Energy industries. Our expertise spans Power Systems Studies, Transmission Lines, Substations, Telecommunications, Protection, Control & Automation, Renewable Energy Connections, Mining, and Engineering, Protection Panel Design and Installation, 3D Design and Manufacturing as well as Construction/Management (EPC/M) services.

We have outstanding opportunity for an experienced Telecommunications Technologist to join and bring their expertise, integrity, and a positive can-do attitude to our dedicated team of professionals.

Position Overview
The Telecommunications Technologist is responsible for designing, implementing, maintaining, and troubleshooting telecommunications systems and networks. This position ensures the reliable operation of voice, data, and video communications across the organisation, supporting both internal and external connectivity requirements.

Key Responsibilities
Install, configure, and maintain telecommunications equipment and systems, including routers, switches, fiber optic cables, PBX, VoIP, and wireless technologies
Installing routers, switches, fiber optic cables, and telephone systems
Monitor and optimise the performance of telecommunications networks and troubleshoot issues to ensure optimal operation and minimal downtime
Collaborate with IT and other departments to integrate telecommunications solutions that meet business needs
Conduct tests and measurements on telecommunications equipment and networks
Conduct regular system upgrades and apply security protocols to safeguard communications infrastructure and ensuring compliance with safety standards
Provide technical support and training to end-users regarding telecommunications equipment and services
Document system configurations, network diagrams, maintenance repairs, and procedures for ongoing reference and compliance
Stay up-to-date with emerging technologies and industry best practices

Key Selection Criteria
Relevant tertiary qualifications in telecommunications, information technology, or a related field
Proven experience in managing and maintaining telecommunications networks and systems
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to resolve complex technical issues
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with a customer-focused approach
Knowledge of Australian telecommunications standards and regulatory requirements

Desirable Attributes
Experience with cloud-based communications platforms
Ability to work independently and as part of a team
Strong organisational skills and attention to detail

If you have the skills required for this role and you feel this is the job for you, then apply now!
Salary: Between $80,000 - $100,000 per annum + Super
